channel.title: Post-Trap Futurism: The Catalog Sessions
channel.description: A limited-run series from Cumulative Web Inc telling the story of That Boy Hi Hat's catalog — one track per episode, plus an origin-story opener. Hosts Marcus and Nia walk through where each song came from, how it was made, and why it sounds like the future.

item.title: Episode 1: Origin Story — Post-Trap Futurism
item.description: There is an independent rapper out of Frederick, Maryland with twenty four songs, his own sound, and a story nobody has told properly yet. This show is going to tell it, one track at a time. Welcome to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Over the next twenty five episodes, we are walking through the entire catalog of That Boy Hi Hat. Not just the hits. Every song. Where it came from, how it was made, and why it sounds like the future. And at the end of every episode, you hear the song itself, start to finish. No clips, no teases. The whole thing. Before we get to track one, you need the origin story. Because this catalog did not happen by accident.

item.title: Episode 2: Diabolique — The Spearhead
item.description: Every catalog has a spearhead. One song the whole operation points at and says, this is the sound, this is the standard. For That Boy Hi Hat, that song is Diabolique. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode two, and we are going deep on one track. Diabolique. The single, the statement, the song carrying the October campaign. Let us set the scene. Cue Recording Studio, Arlington, Virginia. A real room, real engineers, the kind of place where records get made the expensive way. That is where Diabolique was born. Production by Hybrid, who also mixed and mastered it. If you listened to episode one, that name should ring a bell.

item.title: Episode 3: Zooted Zone — The Breakout
item.description: Three hundred seven thousand plays. One song. That is the number that changed everything for That Boy Hi Hat, and the song is Zooted Zone. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode three, and we are telling the story of the breakout. The record that proved an independent catalog out of Maryland could travel. Let us start with the facts, because the facts are the story. Zooted Zone has pulled around three hundred seven thousand lifetime plays on Spotify. The artist was sitting under two hundred monthly listeners. One song carried the entire catalog on its back. And here is how it was made. February of twenty twenty-three.

item.title: Episode 4: Shaka Zulu — The Warrior Code
item.description: Some songs borrow a crown. This one was born wearing it. Shaka Zulu, episode four. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Today we are on the warrior record. The one that reaches back centuries to move forward. Shaka Zulu. The name belongs to the founder of the Zulu Kingdom, one of the most formidable military minds in African history. When a rapper takes that name for a song, he is not being casual. He is declaring what the record is about. Power, strategy, legacy. And the lyrics carry that weight. The song moves through Ethiopia, through midnight in Morocco, through graveyards and Persia. It is a tour of ancient power.

item.title: Episode 5: Doves & Diamonds — Peace and Pressure
item.description: Doves mean peace. Diamonds mean pressure. This song is about what happens when you want both at the same time. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode five. Doves and Diamonds. Let us start with the title, because the title is the whole song. A dove is the oldest symbol of peace there is. A diamond is what you get when peace is not an option, when carbon gets squeezed until it shines. This record lives in the tension between those two things. Wanting the calm. Living in the pressure. Every independent artist knows that tension. You want the soft life, but you are built in the hard one. The song does not resolve it.

item.title: Episode 6: Flex My Flame — Turn It Up
item.description: There is a moment in every artist's run when they stop introducing themselves and start announcing themselves. This is that record. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode six. Flex My Flame. Let us break the title down. To flex is to show your strength on purpose. Not by accident, not humbly. Deliberately. And the flame is the fire, the thing you carry that nobody gave you. Flex My Flame is a song about displaying the fire. No apology in it. Every catalog needs this record. The one where the artist plants a flag. Not the breakout, not the deep cut. The statement of self. When this song comes on, there is no question who made it or why.

item.title: Episode 7: Flamerz — The Producer's Fire
item.description: Behind every flame there is someone who lit the match. Today we meet the producer. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode seven. Flamerz. The title tells you the temperature. Plural. Not one flame. Flames. This is the record where the fire multiplies, and the reason it does is sitting behind the boards. Flamerz was produced by Jeck Da General. That credit matters. Jeck Da General is a producer Black Lansky has built with before, a collaborator in the truest sense. When a label head and a producer have history, the records carry it. You can hear trust in a beat.

item.title: Episode 8: Ultimate — The Last Word
item.description: It is the biggest title in the catalog. One word. Ultimate. You do not name a song that unless you mean it. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode eight. Ultimate. Let us sit with the audacity of that title for a moment. Ultimate means final. The last word. The thing nothing comes after. In a catalog of twenty four songs, naming one of them Ultimate is a claim. It says, this is the definitive article. And the claim is the content. A song called Ultimate does not have to be the best song. It has to be the most certain one. It is the artist looking at his own catalog and saying, this is what I am, all the way.

item.title: Episode 9: Spirits n Shadows — The Haunted House
item.description: Every catalog has a haunted house. This is the address. Spirits n Shadows. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode nine. And we are going to the darkest room in the catalog. The title is a warning. Spirits and shadows. Not one or the other. Both. The things that haunt you and the things that follow you. This is the record where the artist stops performing strength and admits what is in the house with him. The lyrics read like a midnight transmission. A haunted trap house. Souls and spirits. A white wolf pulling the moon out of the sky. It is surreal, but it is not random.

item.title: Episode 10: Painted Lady — The Portrait
item.description: Every catalog has a portrait. One song where the artist stops, looks at someone, and paints. This is the frame. Painted Lady. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode ten. The muse song. A painted lady. The image is old and rich. A woman as a work of art. Someone worth stopping for, worth studying, worth a whole song. In a catalog full of warriors and flames and shadows, this is the record that looks at someone else. And that shift matters. Nine episodes in, we have heard the artist talk about himself in every register. Power, confidence, dread, fire. Now the lens turns outward. A portrait song is a generosity.

item.title: Episode 11: Toxic Element — The Warning Label
item.description: The periodic table has a warning section. This song lives in it. Toxic Element. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode eleven. The dangerous chemistry. An element is basic. Fundamental. The stuff everything is made of. Toxic means it can hurt you. Put them together and you get the most honest love song structure in rap. Attraction to the thing that is bad for you. Every catalog needs this record because every life has this element. The person, the habit, the scene that you know is poison and you reach for anyway. It is not a moral song. It is a chemical one. It describes a reaction, not a decision.

item.title: Episode 12: 7th Angel — Seven Days of Sorrow
item.description: In the Book of Revelation, the seventh angel sounds the trumpet and the mystery is finished. This song starts where that leaves off. Seventh Angel. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode twelve. The most biblical record in the catalog. Seven days of sorrow. That is the refrain the song keeps returning to. I saw the angels falling. I need a demon slayer. I forgot to save my prayers. At the crucifixion, I was cross-faded. This is spiritual warfare set to a beat. Let us take the imagery seriously, because the song does. Angels falling is not a metaphor for a bad week. It is the collapse of the heavenly order.

item.title: Episode 13: Phantasm — The Mirror
item.description: A phantasm is a ghost. An illusion. Something you see that is not there. Or something that is there that you cannot quite see. This song is both. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode thirteen. Phantasm. The mirror record. The central image is the mirror. I keep disappearing when I am gazing in the mirror. I vanish in reflection when the dark night rises. Think about that. Not disappearing in the dark. Disappearing in the mirror. The self, looked at directly, will not hold still. It is one of the most psychologically sharp images in the catalog. The mirror is supposed to show you who you are. Here it shows you vanishing.

item.title: Episode 14: Golden Diamond — Priceless
item.description: Priceless. World class. Golden diamond. When the hook is an affirmation, the song is a mirror that shows you shining. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode fourteen. Golden Diamond. The refrain is the song. Priceless, golden diamond. World class, golden diamond. Repeated until it is not a boast anymore. It is a belief. Say something enough times with enough conviction and it stops being a lyric. It becomes a fact. That is how affirmations work, and this is the catalog's affirmation anthem. Not the flex, which is about showing. The affirmation, which is about becoming. Flex My Flame showed the fire.

item.title: Episode 15: Broken Hearts Club — The Membership
item.description: The membership nobody applied for. The club everybody has been in. Broken Hearts Club. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode fifteen. The most human record in the catalog. Broken hearts club, I have been there before. That is the hook, and it is a confession and an invitation at the same time. A confession, because the artist admits the damage. An invitation, because he is telling you that you are not alone in it. The lyrics do not flinch. Bleeding for redemption. Bleeding from the eyes. Mixing up addictions. Switching my dimensions. Days I hate it here. Blood and scars. Nights I fell apart. This is not heartbreak as a aesthetic.

item.title: Episode 16: Neon Nights Pt. 777 — The Jackpot Night
item.description: Triple seven. The jackpot number. The neon number. The night this record lives in never ends. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode sixteen. Neon Nights Pt. 777. Neon lights, I can take you there. That is the promise of the hook, and it is the oldest promise in nightlife. Follow me. The night has something for you. The song is an invitation to the glow. The lyrics paint the city as a dreamscape. Neon lights. Strobe lights spinning. Ice chains. Colors. A room gone foggy. It is not a specific place. It is every night out that ever felt infinite, compressed into one track. And the seven seventy seven matters.

item.title: Episode 17: Warped & Wicked — The Beautiful Bend
item.description: The file said Worked and Wicked. The artist said otherwise. This is the story of a title, and the strangest trip in the catalog. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode seventeen. Warped and Wicked. First, the title, because the title has a story. The working file was labeled Worked and Wicked. But Black Lansky, the label head, corrected it. The real title is Warped and Wicked. Warped, as in bent out of shape. That one-word correction changes the whole song. Worked and wicked is a resume. Warped and wicked is a state of mind. The correction tells you what the record actually is. Not a story about labor. A transmission from somewhere bent.

item.title: Episode 18: Rainbows And Roses — The Color
item.description: After every storm in this catalog, there is a record like this waiting. Rainbows and Roses. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode eighteen. The color after the storm. The lyrics start in the dark. Sorrows and sins. A chamber of secrets. Eyes full of lies. Screaming at the skies. Make me feel alive. That is where the song begins, in the same shadows we have been walking through for episodes. And then the turn. I left the black hole, feeling color-fly. Candy paint the sky, I praise the sunrise. The song does not deny the darkness. It moves through it. The rainbow is not the absence of the storm. It is what the storm leaves behind.

item.title: Episode 19: Place I Go to Dream — The Escape Hatch
item.description: Everybody has one. A place that only exists when the eyes close. This song is the address. Place I Go to Dream. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode nineteen. The escape hatch. Way above the clouds. That is the refrain, and it is the whole song in four words. The artist is not on the ground for this one. He is up where the air is thin and the view is wide. The lyrics read like a dream journal. Purple rain, each drop telling a story. Shadows in the night. The eyes of a sorceress. Fangs of a viper. It is surreal, but dreams are surreal. The song is not trying to make sense. It is trying to make sleep. And the craft detail is real.

item.title: Episode 20: Scorpions & Sapphires — The Sting and the Shine
item.description: The scorpion stings. The sapphire shines. This song refuses to choose. Scorpions and Sapphires. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode twenty. The venom and the velvet. It is the catalog's signature title construction, and by now you know the pattern. Two things that should not go together. Danger and luxury. The sting and the shine. Doves and diamonds. Rainbows and roses. Now scorpions and sapphires, the sharpest version of the pairing. A scorpion is all warning. It does not pretend to be safe. A sapphire is all allure. It does not pretend to be cheap. Put them in one title and you get the artist's whole philosophy. Be dangerous.

item.title: Episode 21: Tears and Scars — The Testimonial
item.description: Tears evaporate. Scars do not. This song is about what stays. Tears and Scars. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode twenty one. The testimonial. The title is a timeline. Tears are the present tense of pain. They happen now, they fall now. Scars are the past tense. They are what the tears left behind. The song covers the whole arc, from the crying to the mark. And the mark is the point. Anybody can cry. The scar is the proof that you survived the thing that made you cry. This is pain with receipts. The catalog has done heartbreak, has done shadows, has done sorrow. This is the record that shows the tissue. There is a lineage here.

item.title: Episode 22: Smokin' Pain — The Remedy
item.description: The remedy and the wound, in the same title. The medicine with the side effect built in. Smokin Pain. Welcome back to Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode twenty two. The coping record. Smoking the pain. The image is ancient. Fire as medicine. Breath as ritual. The title does not moralize about it. It just names the transaction. There is pain. There is smoke. They meet. And the numbers tell you it is not a dirge. Around eighty eight beats per minute, high danceability, moderate energy. item.title: Episode 25: Tiempo — Time
item.description: Tiempo. It is Spanish for time. And it is the last word of this series. Twenty five episodes. One word to close them. Welcome to the finale of Post-Trap Futurism, the Catalog Sessions. I am Nia. And I am Marcus. Episode twenty five. Tiempo. Time is the subject the whole catalog has been circling. The breakout took years. The spearhead took a studio built over a career. The scars took a lifetime. Every song in this series is a timestamp, and this one names the clock itself. Tiempo in Spanish carries weight that time in English sometimes does not. It is time as weather, as season, as the thing you live inside. Not the clock on the wall. The era. The moment.
